# Job `queue-ask`, Attempt 2: Reviewer feedback on Attempt 1 (rejected)

Attempt 1 (branch `cpd/v0--queue-ask-a1`, commit `c51cabb`, report `/tmp/cpd-build/reports/queue-ask-a1.md`) is correct except for the findings below. **Start from it:** `git cherry-pick c51cabb` in your new worktree. Fix only what is listed, keep everything else as is, and keep the Gate green.

## Reviewer feedback (verbatim)

Acceptance item 4 is not proven. In test/queue/queue.test.ts, the test 'a reader racing 200 writes never sees a partial .json' runs the reader as an async loop in the SAME Node thread as the writer. notifyLead is fully synchronous (writeFileSync then renameSync) and the reader only runs when the writer yields via setImmediate, so the reader can never observe a half-written file. A non-atomic notifyLead that wrote directly to the final .json path would pass this test. Fix: (1) Run the reader truly concurrently, in a separate spawned node process or a worker_thread. It loops readdirSync/readFileSync/JSON.parse/LeadMessageSchema.parse on every name ending in .json, treats ENOENT as fine, collects any other error or parse failure, and reports the problems when told to stop. Start it and wait for a 'running' signal, then do the 200 notifyLead writes in the main process (keep the large text payload so a torn write is likely), then stop it and assert: no problems, the reader read a non-trivial number of files while the writes were happening, 201 .json files in total, all of them schema-valid, and no .tmp files left. (2) Show the test can fail: temporarily change notifyLead to writeFileSync straight to the final path, run the test, confirm it fails, record that transcript in the report, then restore the atomic code. Everything else (ask/answer semantics, exit codes, escalation file protocol, file ownership, gate) is fine and should be left as is. Optional: in the report's Deviations section, state explicitly that escalation ids are reused after a timed-out question is removed (max existing + 1), since a Lead holding a stale answer command could then answer a newer question with the same id.

## Lead addition (contract change, already in `docs/cli-contract.md` §11 `cpd ask`)

Escalation ids must never be reused. On timeout, and in `expireOrphans`, **rename** the question file to `<esc-id>.expired.json` instead of deleting it. `nextEscalationId` must count every existing file for the Attempt (open, answered and expired). `listOpenQuestions` ignores expired ones, and a later `answer` to an expired id gives `escalation_missing`, as before. Update the tests accordingly.
